Self-actualization is visible when someone's life starts to feel like an increasingly accurate expression of their capacities rather than a series of accommodations.
It often looks like depth, integration, and the courage to grow into a form that was only partly available before.

values.name: Self-Awareness
values.description: Understanding your own thoughts, feelings, and actions to improve yourself and your relationships with others.
values.example: Through journaling and reflection, he developed self-awareness about how his communication style affected others, allowing him to make positive changes.
inTheWild: Through journaling and reflection, he developed self-awareness about how his communication style affected others, allowing him to make positive changes.
Self-awareness shows up when someone can name what they are feeling, what story they are telling, and how they are affecting the room.
You notice it in the moment a person catches their own pattern early enough to choose differently.

values.name: Self-Compassion
values.description: Being kind and understanding to yourself during tough times or when you make mistakes.
values.example: After missing an important deadline, she practiced self-compassion by acknowledging her disappointment without harsh self-criticism, then focusing on what she could learn.
inTheWild: After missing an important deadline, she practiced self-compassion by acknowledging her disappointment without harsh self-criticism, then focusing on what she could learn.
Self-compassion shows up when someone talks to themselves like a person worth helping, not a problem worth punishing.
It often looks like taking responsibility without adding cruelty: rest where rest is needed, repair where repair is possible, perspective where shame wants to take over.

values.name: Self-control
values.description: The ability to manage your emotions, thoughts, and behaviors to achieve goals and make good choices.
values.example: Despite feeling angry about the unfair criticism, he demonstrated self-control by taking a deep breath, responding calmly, and addressing the issue constructively.
inTheWild: Choosing to eat a healthy meal instead of giving in to cravings for junk food.
Taking a deep breath and counting to ten before responding in a heated argument.
Resisting the urge to check your phone during a conversation or meeting.

values.name: Selflessness
values.description: Putting the needs and feelings of others before your own and helping them without expecting anything in return.
values.example: The volunteer showed selflessness by spending her vacation building homes in disaster-affected areas rather than taking a personal holiday.
inTheWild: Holding the door open for someone else, even if it means waiting a few extra seconds.
Offering to help a neighbor carry groceries or shovel snow without expecting anything in return.
Donating clothes or household items to a local shelter or charity.

values.name: Service
values.description: Helping others by providing assistance, support, or care.
values.example: The restaurant's commitment to service was evident in how staff remembered regular customers' preferences and went beyond expectations to create special experiences.
inTheWild: Donating clothes or household items to a charity thrift store.

These actions all involve helping others and making a positive impact, even in small ways. By recognizing these simple acts of service, individuals can begin to incorporate this value into their own lives and make a difference in their communities.
The restaurant's commitment to service was evident in how staff remembered regular customers' preferences and went beyond expectations to create special experiences.

values.name: Sovereignty
values.description: The ability of a group or country to govern itself and make its own decisions without outside interference.
values.example: The indigenous community fought to maintain sovereignty over their ancestral lands, ensuring they could make decisions about resource use and development.
inTheWild: The indigenous community fought to maintain sovereignty over their ancestral lands, ensuring they could make decisions about resource use and development.
Sovereignty becomes visible wherever a person or people insist on retaining authority over their own life, land, body, or governance.
It often sharpens under pressure, when outside power assumes it has the right to decide on someone else's behalf.

values.name: Spirituality
values.description: A deep connection to something greater than oneself, often involving personal beliefs and practices that provide meaning and purpose in life.
values.example: She nurtured her spirituality through regular meditation, time in nature, and participating in a community that shared her belief in interconnectedness.
inTheWild: She nurtured her spirituality through regular meditation, time in nature, and participating in a community that shared her belief in interconnectedness.
Spirituality becomes visible in the practices and perceptions that keep a person in contact with what they experience as sacred, ultimate, or deeply meaningful.
You notice it in ritual, reverence, surrender, wonder, and in the way belief shapes ordinary ethics.

values.name: Sports
values.description: Activities that involve physical exertion and skill, often played individually or in teams for competition or enjoyment.
values.example: The community invested in sports programs that taught children not just athletic skills but also teamwork, perseverance, and fair play.
inTheWild: The community invested in sports programs that taught children not just athletic skills but also teamwork, perseverance, and fair play.
Sports become visible not only in competition but in the culture around training, effort, discipline, teamwork, and recovery.
You see their value in how people learn to lose, win, cooperate, endure, and care about excellence in public.

values.name: Sportsmanship
values.description: Treating opponents with respect and fairness, showing graciousness in winning or losing.
values.example: After the championship game, the losing team demonstrated excellent sportsmanship by sincerely congratulating the winners and thanking the officials.
inTheWild: Holding the door open for someone, even if they are your opponent in a game or competition.
Congratulating someone on their success, even if it means they have surpassed you in a particular activity.
Helping someone who is struggling or having a difficult time, even if it means sacrificing your own success or advancement.

values.name: Stability
values.description: Staying steady and balanced in difficult situations without being easily shaken or changed.
values.example: During the company merger, the manager provided stability by maintaining regular team meetings, clear communication, and consistent expectations.
inTheWild: A table that doesn't wobble when you place items on it is an example of stability in everyday life.
A building that remains standing in the face of strong winds or earthquakes is an example of stability.
A bicycle that remains upright and balanced while in motion is an example of stability.

values.name: Stewardship
values.description: Caring for and managing resources responsibly to ensure their health and availability for the future.
values.example: The family farm practiced stewardship by using sustainable methods that preserved soil health and biodiversity for future generations.
inTheWild: The family farm practiced stewardship by using sustainable methods that preserved soil health and biodiversity for future generations.
Stewardship shows up when someone treats a resource, role, place, or inheritance as something to tend rather than consume.
You notice it in maintenance, restraint, repair, and decisions made on behalf of people who are not in the room yet.

values.name: Stillness
values.description: A state of calmness and peace that allows for clear thinking and reflection.
values.example: Before making major decisions, she sought stillness through meditation and quiet walks in nature, allowing her to access deeper wisdom.
inTheWild: Before making major decisions, she sought stillness through meditation and quiet walks in nature, allowing her to access deeper wisdom.
Stillness is often the intentional removal of noise so that subtler truths have somewhere to land.
You can feel its value in the room that is not filled, the pause that is not rushed, the mind that is not constantly self-interrupting.

values.name: Strategy
values.description: A plan to achieve specific goals by using available resources effectively.
values.example: Rather than reacting to market changes, the company developed a strategy with clear objectives, resource allocation, and contingency plans.
inTheWild: Rather than reacting to market changes, the company developed a strategy with clear objectives, resource allocation, and contingency plans.
Strategy becomes visible when someone can hold the long game while still making the next move concrete.
It shows up in sequencing, tradeoffs, and the discipline to stop doing things that do not serve the actual objective.

values.name: Sustainability
values.description: The ability to meet our needs today without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs.
values.example: The building was designed with sustainability in mind, using renewable energy, water reclamation systems, and materials with minimal environmental impact.
inTheWild: Recycling plastic bottles to reduce waste and conserve resources.
Using public transportation or carpooling to reduce carbon emissions and promote sustainable transportation.
Turning off lights and electronics when not in use to conserve energy and reduce electricity consumption.

values.name: Synergy
values.description: Working together in a way that creates better results than individuals could achieve alone.
values.example: The marketing and product development teams achieved synergy by collaborating closely, resulting in innovations that better met customer needs than either could create independently.
inTheWild: The marketing and product development teams achieved synergy by collaborating closely, resulting in innovations that better met customer needs than either could create independently.
Synergy is what happens when different strengths stop competing for dominance and start compounding.
You notice it when the combination produces something neither side could have generated alone.

values.name: Teaching
values.description: Helping others learn new things through guidance and sharing knowledge.
values.example: The mentor excelled at teaching by adapting her approach to each person's learning style and creating opportunities for hands-on practice.
inTheWild: The mentor excelled at teaching by adapting her approach to each person's learning style and creating opportunities for hands-on practice.
Teaching shows up when someone can feel the gap between what they know and what another person can currently take in.
It becomes visible in pacing, examples, questions, and the patience to stay until understanding actually lands.

values.name: Teamwork
values.description: Working together with others to achieve a common goal and support each other.
values.example: The emergency response demonstrated excellent teamwork as medical staff, firefighters, and police coordinated their efforts seamlessly to save lives.
inTheWild: A sports team working together to win a game, with each player contributing their unique skills to the team's success.
A group of coworkers collaborating on a project, sharing ideas and supporting each other to achieve a common goal.
A group of friends coming together to plan and execute a surprise party for someone, with each person taking on a specific task to ensure the party is a success.

values.name: Technology
values.description: The use of scientific knowledge and tools to solve problems and improve lives.
values.example: The organization leveraged technology to connect isolated elderly individuals with healthcare providers and family members during the pandemic.
inTheWild: The organization leveraged technology to connect isolated elderly individuals with healthcare providers and family members during the pandemic.
You see technology when a team automates a repetitive task, uses a tool to extend what they can do, or chooses a better system over more manual work.
It shows up when someone reaches for a product, platform, or workflow to reduce friction, increase access, or connect people at a distance.

values.name: Thoughtfulness
values.description: Showing care and consideration for others' feelings and needs in every action and decision.
values.example: The manager demonstrated thoughtfulness by remembering team members' professional goals and creating opportunities aligned with their aspirations.
inTheWild: Holding the door open for someone behind you, or offering to help someone carry a heavy load up the stairs.
Taking the time to listen to a friend or family member who is going through a tough time, and offering support and guidance where possible.
Letting someone go ahead of you in line at the grocery store, or allowing someone to merge into traffic ahead of you while driving.

values.name: Tolerance
values.description: Respecting and accepting differences in others, even when you don't agree with them.
values.example: The community practiced tolerance by creating spaces where people of different faiths could share their traditions and learn from each other respectfully.
inTheWild: The community practiced tolerance by creating spaces where people of different faiths could share their traditions and learn from each other respectfully.
Tolerance becomes visible when difference does not trigger immediate punishment, erasure, or control.
You notice it in the restraint to let another person exist fully without needing them to mirror you.

values.name: Tranquility
values.description: A settled calm that creates spaciousness, steadiness, and ease in the midst of daily life.
values.example: After a tense morning, she restored tranquility by stepping away from notifications, taking a slow walk outside, and returning to her work with a quieter nervous system.
inTheWild: After a tense morning, she restored tranquility by stepping away from notifications, taking a slow walk outside, and returning to her work with a quieter nervous system.
Tranquility shows up when someone protects a little silence, margin, or softness instead of feeding the next wave of urgency.
You notice it in an unhurried room, a regulated body, and the choice to move gently when speed would only create more noise.

values.name: Travel
values.description: Moving through new places in ways that expand perspective, invite discovery, and break the spell of the familiar.
values.example: He honored travel by planning a solo trip through three small coastal towns, leaving enough room in the schedule to wander, talk with locals, and let the place change his pace.
inTheWild: He honored travel by planning a solo trip through three small coastal towns, leaving enough room in the schedule to wander, talk with locals, and let the place change his pace.
Travel becomes visible in the choice to leave the known long enough to be surprised by another landscape, rhythm, or way of living.
You notice it in packed bags, changed routes, and the willingness to be briefly disoriented so the world can feel larger again.

values.name: Trust
values.description: Being honest and reliable with others creates a strong bond and encourages openness.
values.example: The leader built trust by consistently following through on commitments, admitting mistakes, and sharing information transparently with the team.
inTheWild: When a parent hands over their car keys to their teenage child for the first time, trusting that they will drive responsibly and safely.
When an employer delegates an important task to an employee, trusting that they will complete it on time and to the best of their ability.
When a friend confides in another friend, trusting that they will keep the information confidential.

values.name: Truth
values.description: Being honest and accurate, reflecting reality without lies or deceit.
values.example: The journalist pursued truth by verifying facts with multiple sources and presenting findings even when they contradicted popular narratives.
inTheWild: The journalist pursued truth by verifying facts with multiple sources and presenting findings even when they contradicted popular narratives.
Truth becomes expensive when the facts threaten identity, convenience, status, or belonging; that is usually where its value is clearest.
You see it in verification, correction, and the refusal to keep a useful lie alive.

values.name: Unity
values.description: Bringing people together to work towards a common goal and support each other.
values.example: The community crisis center fostered unity by creating structures for neighbors from different backgrounds to work together on shared challenges.
inTheWild: The community crisis center fostered unity by creating structures for neighbors from different backgrounds to work together on shared challenges.
Unity becomes real when people can coordinate around a common good without pretending they are all the same.
It shows up in solidarity that can survive difference, tension, and shared responsibility.

values.name: Versatility
values.description: The ability to adapt to new situations and handle different tasks effectively.
values.example: The small business owner demonstrated versatility by quickly pivoting to online services when in-person operations became impossible during the pandemic.
inTheWild: The small business owner demonstrated versatility by quickly pivoting to online services when in-person operations became impossible during the pandemic.
Versatility shows up when someone can carry their usefulness across contexts instead of needing the conditions to stay familiar.
You notice it in people who can switch modes, learn fast, and remain effective when the shape of the work changes.

values.name: Vision
values.description: Creating a clear and inspiring picture of the future that guides decisions and motivates people.
values.example: The founder's vision of affordable healthcare for all communities guided the organization's growth and strategic partnerships for decades.
inTheWild: Planning a vacation: When you plan a vacation, you are creating a vision of the future that is exciting and motivational. You imagine yourself in a new place, experiencing new things, and this vision helps you save money, make plans, and get through the daily grind.

Decorating your home: When you decorate your home, you are creating a vision of the future that is beautiful and inspiring. You imagine a space that is comfortable, welcoming, and reflective of your personality, and this vision helps you choose colors, furniture, and accessories that bring that vision to life.

Setting goals: When you set goals for yourself, you are creating a vision of the future that is challenging and rewarding. You imagine yourself achieving something that is important to you, and this vision helps you stay motivated, focused, and on track.

values.name: Willingness
values.description: A readiness to do what is needed or to accept new ideas and experiences.
values.example: When the project faced unexpected challenges, the team's willingness to adjust their approach and learn new skills allowed them to succeed despite the obstacles.
inTheWild: Trying a new hobby or activity that is outside of one's comfort zone, such as taking up a new sport or learning a new skill.
Taking on a challenging project at work or in school that requires a willingness to learn new things and take on new responsibilities.
Being open to feedback and constructive criticism, and using it as an opportunity to improve and grow.

values.name: Wisdom
values.description: The ability to make good decisions based on knowledge, experience, and understanding.
values.example: The elder demonstrated wisdom by listening carefully before offering advice that considered both immediate needs and long-term implications.
inTheWild: A teacher who takes the time to understand each student's individual learning style and adapts their teaching approach accordingly, demonstrating sound judgment and insight.
A friend who listens attentively and offers thoughtful advice when faced with a problem, showing an ability to analyze a situation and provide thoughtful guidance.
A doctor who takes a holistic approach to treating a patient, considering their physical, emotional, and mental well-being, demonstrating a wise and compassionate approach to healthcare.

values.name: Work Ethic
values.description: Having a strong work ethic means being dedicated, responsible, and putting in effort to complete tasks well.
values.example: Her work ethic was evident in how she consistently arrived early, gave full attention to quality details, and willingly helped colleagues complete team projects.
inTheWild: Her work ethic was evident in how she consistently arrived early, gave full attention to quality details, and willingly helped colleagues complete team projects.
Work ethic becomes visible in consistency when no one is supervising and in standards that do not disappear under stress.
It often looks like reliability, thoroughness, and the choice to finish well instead of merely being seen trying.
